youtubeTitle: The Gospel and Soul Health Session 3 - Dr Bruce Wauchope
chapter: 1st Non-negotiable (cont): The Love and Indivisible Union of Father, Son and Spirit (The Who); 2nd Non-negotiable: The Dream, The Pre-Creation Story, Our Purpose, Sons and Daughters of God (The Why)
topic: The pre-creation dream: adopted as children
summary: Bruce first clarifies that we are never without Christ: the whole universe is held together by his life (zoe), even though in our darkness we experience God as coming from outside. No one knows the Father except the Son, yet the Father, Son and Spirit are in everyone, so the problem lies in human blindness, not in God. He then lays down the second non-negotiable, 'the Why': before creation, the Father, Son and Spirit purposed to include us in their love as sons and daughters, a grace given in Christ 'before time began'. That pre-creation purpose is the backdrop against which everything in creation, including God's wrath, must be measured. Jesus died not to satisfy an angry Father but because we killed him; he submitted to us so that he could reach the bottom of human darkness and bring the Father's love into every person. Our calling and identity is to be placed in the middle of the Trinity's flow of love.
keyPoints: We are never without Christ. All things are held together by his zoe, though in our darkness the Spirit seems to come from outside.
'No one knows the Father except the Son' (Matthew 11, Luke 10, John 1, 6, 7). Yet the Trinity is in everyone, so the problem is human blindness, not a problem with Dad.
The Father, Son and Spirit are one yet distinct, and love needs distinction: love doesn't happen in porridge.
The second non-negotiable is the Why: the Trinity's purpose for creation is children. They want relationship with distinct beings, all held within them.
Titus 1:2 says eternal life, which is knowing the Father and the Son (John 17:3), was promised before time began, not after we confessed or were baptised.
2 Timothy 1:9-10 says we were saved and called by grace given in Christ before time began, not according to our works, and Christ has abolished death.
Ephesians 1:4-5: we were chosen in him before the foundation of the world and predestined for adoption as children.

This pre-creation purpose is the measure for everything that happens in creation, including God's wrath. Bruce compares it to his fussy levelling of a sloping yard, which only made sense once you knew he was building a playground for his kids.
Looking down on 'the dregs of humanity' is how the higher angelic powers speak. The Father, Son and Spirit love the bottom and go to the bottom.
Jesus died because we killed him and he submitted to us, so that he could reach every human and bring the Father's love. He did not die to satisfy an angry God.
The early church's Trinity diagrams show the flow of love: the Father loves the Son in the Spirit. Our calling is to be in the middle of that love (John 17:26).
Since Christ is underneath the darkest parts of us, we can move towards and even embrace parts of ourselves we fear. The gospel is about the heart and soul, not tithes and good behaviour.

keyTerms.definition: The life of Christ that holds every person and the whole universe together.
The first non-negotiable: Father, Son and Spirit, one and distinct, loving one another.
The second non-negotiable: the pre-creation purpose to have sons and daughters included in the Trinity's love.
Not mere endless existence but knowing the Father and the Son and receiving their love (John 17:3).
The Trinity's dream and decision, before time began, to include humanity in Christ.
A calling 'not of this cosmos': the uncreated, loving call of the Trinity.
The attitude of higher powers that despise humanity's weakness and cannot imagine God loving it.

quotes: Love doesn't happen in porridge. Love happens when you've got distinction.
Grace given to us in Christ Jesus. After I believed? No. Before time began!
Jesus died because we killed him, and he submitted himself to us.
Maybe those parts of me I'm scared of are loved and held by Jesus.

caseStudy.title: "Was I a mistake?"
caseStudy.scenario: Daniel, 28, grew up hearing that his birth was unplanned, and he has always felt like an inconvenience. He tries hard to be useful so that people will keep him around. When he fails, he concludes that God, like his family, only puts up with him. He avoids looking at his own feelings because they seem shameful.
caseStudy.analysis: Daniel measures his worth by his circumstances and his performance. Bruce's second non-negotiable reverses this: before time began, the Father, Son and Spirit wanted Daniel as a son, and grace was given to him in Christ then, not according to his works. The pre-creation purpose, not his family story, is the true backdrop, and Christ is beneath even the parts of himself Daniel avoids.
pathway: Read 2 Timothy 1:9 and Ephesians 1:4-5 daily for a month, putting his own name into them.
Name the story 'I'm an inconvenience' and set it against 'wanted before time began'.
Practise turning gently towards one difficult feeling a day, imagining Christ beneath it.
Notice the urge to earn his place, and choose one moment each week simply to receive instead.
Consider working through family-of-origin pain with a qualified counsellor.

practices.name: Before-time meditation
practices.how: Sit quietly and imagine the Father, Son and Spirit before creation, delighting in the idea of you. Say: 'I was wanted before anything began.'

practices.name: Measure against the backdrop
practices.how: When something painful happens, ask: 'How does this look against the Trinity's purpose to include me as their child?'

practices.name: Turning towards
practices.how: Choose a part of yourself you avoid, and prayerfully imagine Jesus holding it from underneath, for five minutes.

reflection: How does knowing you were chosen 'before time began' affect the way you see your failures?
Where have you taken on the 'angelic' view that looks down on weak or broken people, including yourself?
What part of yourself might you begin to embrace if Christ is already holding it?

quiz.q: What is the second non-negotiable, 'the Why'?
options: The Trinity's pre-creation purpose to have sons and daughters
quiz.explain: Before creation, the Trinity purposed to include us in their love as children.

quiz.q: According to Titus 1:2, as Bruce reads it, when was eternal life promised?
quiz.explain: God promised it before the ages began, independent of our actions.

quiz.q: Why does Bruce say Jesus died?
options: To pay off an angry Father
Because the Father turned away from sin
Because we killed him, and he submitted to reach the bottom of our darkness
quiz.explain: Jesus submitted to human violence so that the Father's love could be in us.
